named_question: Which stored mode and capability select the per-mood numeric editor rather than packed-color controls, and how does its accepted scalar encode?

static_byte_pins.purpose: Restores the omitted channel-index argument to CapAI getter and binds the 0x40/low-three-bit dispatch and numeric display clamp.
Binds control scalar clamp, selected scene lookup, output bounds, high-nibble preservation and low-payload replacement.

storage_bindings.selected_tag: The selected mood's Qn high nibble, not an unconditional RGB flag or a physical actuator classification.
storage_bindings.payload: The selected primary-vector slot masked with 0x0fffffff.
storage_bindings.capability: For Qn, CapAI<n-1> binds controller+0x20e8+2*(n-1). The getter reads that unsigned 16-bit slot.
storage_bindings.missing_capability: The reader visits capability bindings independently of the nonempty-name write guard. Common attribute read clears its temporary string; absent attribute with this binding's param7=0 reaches type3 conversion, whose empty decimal parse returns0. Inspection still reports raw omission; numeric editing can use the recovered reader default0.
storage_bindings.prior_width_binding: Reuse recovered_count_and_output_contract.sparse_native_read in contracts/light-controller2.json: absent/zero per-scene Outputs means12 on that reader. Stored Qn outside the read width is not used to invent a loaded mode.

per_mood_dialog_dispatch.editor: numeric scalar branch7; displayed low payload capped at100

per_mood_dialog_dispatch.capability: No tag6 remapping at this site

numeric_edit.rule: Native scalar clamps to0..100 then stores (oldQ & 0xf0000000) | scalar in the selected existing primary-vector slot. It does not RGB-pack that scalar, change the type tag or resize the vector.
numeric_edit.color_distinction: Separate color handler0x1400e6590 preserves the old tag and uses0x14043ab40. Its ordinary RGB branch packs percent R + G*1000 + B*1000000; an alternate extended branch and sequence changes also exist. Numeric37 is not RGB37%green or a new type-0 raw37.

separate_effective_mode_helper: Do not replace dialog dispatch with0x1405c1870. That helper starts from the first scene's tag and, for tag6, prioritizes capability0x20->8, then0x40->9, then low-three-bit selection6/7. The per-mood renderer instead starts from the selected scene and does not test0x20 in its tag6 branch. No shared physical/runtime channel-role model is inferred.

CLI_policy.command: lox config lighting set-mood-level FILE BLOCK --mood SID_OR_NAME --output-index N --level 0..100 [--room ROOM] [--save-as PATH]
CLI_policy.selection: Exactly one LightController2, one direct LightscenesC and one direct mood matching exact stored SID spelling or Name. Ambiguous/missing matches fail before mutation.
CLI_policy.supported_inputs: This specific recovered editor's indices1..18, selected stored signed-32-bit Qn within its reader width, and a supported numeric branch. Needed explicit capabilities must be nonnegative16-bit decimals; malformed, negative or out-of-range values are rejected rather than natively truncated. Unneeded capabilities on direct numeric tags are untouched.
CLI_policy.mutation: Reject level outside0..100; never clamp. Preserve old high nibble and replace only selected low payload. Preserve equivalent spelling/no-op bytes, other Qn, IDs, Outputs, Num, sequences, HCL, capabilities, references and unknown data. Existing writer formatting and Document stamps retain their normal behavior.
CLI_policy.compatibility: Existing set-mood-color remains an explicit packed/raw storage edit, not a channel-appropriate numeric operation. No silent change to its previous behavior.

native_validation: The separate numeric-edit-save-reopen-20261111.json records one actually accepted numeric37 edit and fresh native reopen; source rules beyond that case are not relabeled GUI-tested.
limits: Stored per-mood editor-kind validation, not a prediction of graph-dependent pre-modal retagging/capability refresh or physical channel roles.
No complete dialog editability/permission, Num-limited import, special-scene, sequence, dynamic-white, hardware or runtime parity.
Do not reproduce native incidental normalization of other outputs/HCL. Accepted-dialog whole-file equality with a one-field CLI edit is not claimed.
Normal-return source dataflow assumes valid objects, successful helper calls and no unexpected aliases/reentrancy.
